<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Connection Between SLERP and Recall@<math id="A6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math></h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix provides the metric-level details connecting the geometric
SLERP characterization in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> to
Recall@<math id="A6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>. We first define Recall@<math id="A6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> for queries with multiple relevant
gallery items, then introduce a top-<math id="A6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> margin, and finally prove that
angular proximity to a positive-margin direction certifies top-<math id="A6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> retrieval
success.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Recall@<math id="A6.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> with Multiple Relevant Items</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let the deployed gallery be</p>
<table id="A6.E82" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For a query <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{Q}</annotation></semantics></math>, let</p>

<p id="A6.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">denote the set of relevant gallery indices, and let</p>

</table>
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">denote the set of negative indices. We assume <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(x)\neq\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(x)\neq\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A6.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|N(x)|\geq K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|N(x)|\geq K</annotation></semantics></math>. The set <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(x)</annotation></semantics></math> may contain multiple relevant items, as in
image-to-text retrieval with multiple captions per image or in retrieval
benchmarks where several gallery items are valid matches for the same query.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{K}(q)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N_{g}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{K}(q)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N_{g}\}</annotation></semantics></math> be the set of indices of the <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>
highest-scoring gallery items under <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{s_{j}(q)\}_{j=1}^{N_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{s_{j}(q)\}_{j=1}^{N_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math>, with ties
resolved by a fixed deterministic rule. The single-query Recall@<math id="A6.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> event
is</p>
<table id="A6.E86" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A6.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Thus, with multiple relevant items, Recall@<math id="A6.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is a hit indicator: it is
equal to one whenever at least one relevant gallery item appears among the
top <math id="A6.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> retrieved items.</p>

<div id="A6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Since the query direction is input-dependent, dataset-level Recall@<math id="A6.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is
defined for a query rule <math id="A6.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h:\mathcal{Q}\to\mathbb{S}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h:\mathcal{Q}\to\mathbb{S}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A6.E87" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A6.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">For SLERP with fixed interpolation weight <math id="A6.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, the query rule is
<math id="A6.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\alpha}(x)=q_{\alpha}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\alpha}(x)=q_{\alpha}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, and therefore</p>

<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

<p id="A6.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The top-<math id="A6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> retrieval margin is</p>

gallery items. Therefore</span></p>

∎</span></p>

<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Retrieval-Relevant Optimal Direction</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The geometric analysis in the main text is formulated with respect to a
optimal direction <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\ast}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\ast}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. To specialize this direction to
Recall@<math id="A6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, we choose a direction that maximizes the top-<math id="A6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> margin:</p>
<table id="A6.E98" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.E98.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}_{K}(x)\in\arg\max_{q\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}m_{K,x}(q)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>K</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}_{K}(x)\in\arg\max_{q\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}m_{K,x}(q).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(98)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Such a maximizer exists. Indeed, each score <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}(q)=\langle q,g_{j}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{j}(q)=\langle q,g_{j}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>
is continuous in <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. The maximum over finitely many relevant scores is
continuous, and the <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-th order statistic over finitely many negative
scores is also continuous. Hence <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{K,x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{K,x}</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous. Since <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{S}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{S}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is
compact, the maximum is attained.</p>
</div>

serve as a retrieval-relevant optimal direction. With this choice, define
the angular gap</p>

relative interior of the minor arc joining <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|m_{K,x}(q)-m_{K,x}(q^{\prime})|\leq|s_{x}^{+}(q)-s_{x}^{+}(q^{\prime})|+|\tau^{-}_{K,x}(q)-\tau^{-}_{K,x}(q^{\prime})|\leq 2\|q-q^{\prime}\|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(105)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS4.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS4.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, for unit vectors,</span></p>

<div id="A6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since all scores are cosine similarities, they lie in <math id="A6.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence the
difference between any relevant score and any negative score is at most <math id="A6.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>,

<p id="A6.SS5.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS5.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, if</span></p>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Cross-Modal Zero-shot Classification</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate zero-shot classification as an auxiliary evaluation setting.
Class text prototypes are encoded by the old-model text encoder using the template <span id="A7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘‘A photo of a &lt;class_name&gt;’’</span> and kept fixed.
Image embeddings are obtained from the new model either directly via SVD alignment or by applying SLERP to the SVD-aligned embeddings, then compared against the fixed old-model prototypes.
Thus, only the image side changes, while the text-prototype side remains in the old-model space.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For classification, the Procrustes alignment is estimated on ImageNet-1K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">83</a>]</cite> validation set using text-only support.
The SLERP weight <math id="A7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on ImageNet validation top-1 accuracy and then fixed for evaluation on Cars, Pets, Flowers, Aircraft, DTD, EuroSAT, Food101, SUN397, Caltech101, and UCF101.
For SLERP, <math id="A7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to old-model image embeddings, while <math id="A7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to SVD-aligned new-model image embeddings.
We also report <math id="A7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, the dataset-specific oracle weight, as an upper-bound reference.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Tab. <a href="#A7.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Appendix G Cross-Modal Zero-shot Classification ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows that SVD alignment alone recovers a meaningful fraction of the old-model classifier’s accuracy, but remains lower on average. Applying SLERP to the SVD-aligned embeddings consistently improves this endpoint, often closing the gap to, or even surpassing, the old-model classifier. This trend mirrors the retrieval results: SVD provides a useful but approximate alignment between the two model representations, while SLERP yields a more effective representation in the old-model space.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>
Zero-shot classification accuracy (%) with fixed old-model text prototypes.
For SLERP, the support-set-selected weight <math id="A7.T3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on the
ImageNet-1K validation set and fixed across target datasets, whereas
<math id="A7.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected directly on each target dataset and is reported
only as an oracle upper bound.
Bold and underlined values denote the best and second-best classification
results, respectively, excluding the old- and new-model reference rows.
</figcaption>

<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A8.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix H Additional SLERP Arc Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A8.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix H Additional SLERP Arc Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> extend the SLERP analysis to image-to-text Recall@1 on Flickr30k, COCO, and NoCaps.

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A8.F7.sf3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(c)</span> </span><span id="A8.F7.sf3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">NoCaps</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A8.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A8.F7.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A8.F7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Image-to-text Recall@1 along the SLERP path for SigLIP1 <math id="A8.F7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-H/14.</span>
The text gallery is encoded by the old model, while image queries interpolate between the old-model query and the SVD-aligned new-model query.
The case <math id="A8.F7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to old-model queries, while <math id="A8.F7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to SVD-aligned new-model queries.
Markers show the CC3M-selected <math id="A8.F7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> and the dataset-specific test oracle <math id="A8.F7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>; dashed lines show old-model, SVD, and new-model reference performance.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The curves show the same behavior observed in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Compatibility Results ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>.
For both CLIP ViT-H/14 <math id="A8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32 and SigLIP1 <math id="A8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-H/14, the best test performance is typically reached at an interior interpolation weight rather than at either endpoint.
The CC3M validation set curve also follows the test-set curve closely, and the selected <math id="A8.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is near the dataset-specific oracle <math id="A8.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus, the benefit of SLERP is not restricted to text-to-image retrieval: the same support-set selected interpolation also transfers to image-to-text retrieval across datasets and model families.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A8.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="A8.T4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A8.T4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cross-modal backward-compatible retrieval on Flickr30k.</span>

The support-set-selected weight <math id="A8.T4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on CC3M, whereas
<math id="A8.T4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected directly on Flickr30k and is reported only as an
oracle upper bound.
Checkmarks indicate backward compatibility; bold and underlined values denote
the best and second-best <math id="A8.T4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{new}\!\to\!\mathrm{old}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>new</mi><mo lspace="0.128em" rspace="0.128em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>old</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{new}\!\to\!\mathrm{old}</annotation></semantics></math> results, respectively.

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A8.T5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 5</span>: </span><span id="A8.T5.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A8.T5.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cross-modal backward-compatible retrieval on COCO.</span>
The <math id="A8.T5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> column reports the interpolation weights for I2T/T2I retrieval.
The Sup. column indicates the support modality used to estimate the Procrustes map: text-only (T), image-only (I), or joint image–text (I+T).
The support-set-selected weight <math id="A8.T5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on CC3M, whereas
<math id="A8.T5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected directly on COCO and is reported only as an
oracle upper bound.
Checkmarks indicate backward compatibility; bold and underlined values denote
the best and second-best <math id="A8.T5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{new}\!\to\!\mathrm{old}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>new</mi><mo lspace="0.128em" rspace="0.128em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>old</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{new}\!\to\!\mathrm{old}</annotation></semantics></math> results, respectively.

The Sup. column indicates the support modality used to estimate the Procrustes map: text-only (T), image-only (I), or joint image–text (I+T).
The support-set-selected weight <math id="A8.T6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on CC3M, whereas
<math id="A8.T6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected directly on NoCaps and is reported only as an
oracle upper bound.
Checkmarks indicate backward compatibility; bold and underlined values denote
the best and second-best <math id="A8.T6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{new}\!\to\!\mathrm{old}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>new</mi><mo lspace="0.128em" rspace="0.128em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>old</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{new}\!\to\!\mathrm{old}</annotation></semantics></math> results, respectively.

<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Detailed Retrieval Performance</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tabs. <a href="#A8.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Appendix H Additional SLERP Arc Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, <a href="#A8.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Appendix H Additional SLERP Arc Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, and <a href="#A8.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Appendix H Additional SLERP Arc Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> provide the full Recall@1/5/10 metrics for the retrieval settings of the experimental results in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Compatibility Results ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>.
For each dataset, we report both image-to-text (I2T) and text-to-image (T2I) retrieval, for all support modalities used to estimate the Procrustes alignment.
We compare SVD alignment alone, XBT (when available), and SLERP applied to the SVD-aligned embeddings with both the support-set selected weight <math id="A9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> and the dataset-specific oracle <math id="A9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The tables also include the CLIP ViT-H/14 <math id="A9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32 setting, which has been adopted by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">51</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The detailed results confirm the trend of Tables <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
SVD provides a strong new-to-old alignment with no model retraining or gradient-based optimization, but it does not consistently achieve compatibility across model pairs, datasets, and support modalities.
SLERP improves the corresponding SVD endpoint in nearly all settings, and the gains extend beyond Recall@1 to Recall@5 and Recall@10.
This shows that interpolation not only improves the top-ranked item, but also produces a more compatible ranking over the old-model gallery.</p>
</div>
<div id="A9.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The same pattern holds across same-family and cross-family pairs.
In the CLIP same-family settings, SLERP is consistently competitive with the training-based XBT baseline while requiring no compatibility training.
In the cross-family settings, including the difficult SigLIP1 <math id="A9.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-H/14 case, SLERP often turns incompatible SVD rows into compatible ones.
Across support modalities, text-only support remains the most stable overall, while image-only and joint support can be competitive for specific retrieval directions (I2T or T2I).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Re-indexing</h2>

<figure id="A10.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A10.T7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="A10.T7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Reindexed-gallery retrieval for same-family model upgrades.
For each dataset, the <math id="A10.T7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> column reports the interpolation weights for
I2T/T2I retrieval.
The Sup. column indicates the support modality used to estimate the Procrustes map: text-only (T), image-only (I), or joint image–text (I+T).
The support-set-selected weight <math id="A10.T7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on CC3M and fixed
across test datasets, whereas <math id="A10.T7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected directly on each
test dataset and is reported only as an oracle upper bound.
Bold and underlined values denote the best and second-best results,
respectively, excluding the old- and new-model reference rows.
</span></figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A10.T8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="A10.T8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Reindexed-gallery retrieval for cross-family model upgrades.
For each dataset, the <math id="A10.T8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> column reports the interpolation weights for
I2T/T2I retrieval.
The Sup. column indicates the support modality used to estimate the Procrustes map: text-only (T), image-only (I), or joint image–text (I+T).
The support-set-selected weight <math id="A10.T8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on CC3M and fixed
across all test datasets, whereas <math id="A10.T8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected directly on each
test dataset and is reported only as an oracle upper bound.
Bold and underlined values denote the best and second-best results,
respectively, excluding the old- and new-model reference rows.

<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.25.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.25.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="--ltx-bg-color:#EBF4FF;">87.07</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.25.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.25.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline" style="--ltx-bg-color:#EBF4FF;">67.31</span></span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb"><math id="A10.T8.m27" class="ltx_Math" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;" alttext="\blacktriangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;" mathbackground="#F5F5F5">▶</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\blacktriangleright</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;"> New model (SigLIP1)</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">–</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">–</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">58.09</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">39.40</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">–</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">46.99</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">30.88</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">–</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">86.20</span></span>
<span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A10.T8.5.1.1.1.26.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">64.18</span></span></span>
</span>
</span></span></p>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tabs. <a href="#A10.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Appendix J Re-indexing ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and <a href="#A10.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Appendix J Re-indexing ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> report the re-indexing setting, where the gallery is allowed to be re-indexed.
This setting differs from the compatibility evaluation in Eq. <a href="#S4.E15" title="In 4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>, since the gallery is no longer fixed in the old-model space.
Instead, both query and gallery embeddings can be interpolated using the same SLERP weight: <math id="A10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the old-model representations, whereas <math id="A10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the SVD-aligned new-model representations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In this setting, the SVD endpoint is equivalent to evaluating the new model directly.
Because the orthogonal Procrustes map is applied to both query and gallery embeddings, it preserves all pairwise inner products and therefore leaves the retrieval ranking unchanged relative to the new model’s original representation space.
Consequently, the SVD results coincide with the new-model results.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p3.1" class="ltx_p">SLERP often improves over this endpoint, indicating that interpolation can be beneficial even when re-indexing is allowed.
These gains are particularly notable because SLERP requires no model retraining and, in several cases, matches or exceeds XBT, which requires compatibility training.
Overall, these results show that SLERP not only restores compatibility with an existing old-model index, but can also produce stronger interpolated representations when re-indexing is permitted.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A11" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix K </span>Target-Set Budget Sensitivity</h2>

<figure id="A11.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.39836v1/thresh_val_curves_horizontal.png" id="A11.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/134;" width="429" height="134" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A11.F8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="A11.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Recall@1 along the SLERP path under different target-set fractions.
Solid curves report the average over three random seeds; shaded regions denote <math id="A11.F8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> across seeds.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A11.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix K Target-Set Budget Sensitivity ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> examines how much target-distribution data is required to estimate a dataset-specific SLERP weight.
For each target-set fraction, we subsample the target benchmark using three random seeds and compute Recall@1 along the SLERP path.
The solid curves show the mean Recall@1 across seeds, and the shaded regions indicate one standard deviation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Across both model pairs, even small target subsets identify the same high-performing region of the SLERP curve.
Reducing the target-set budget increases the variance of the Recall@1 estimates, but the maximizer remains stable and close to that obtained using the full target set.
This suggests that a reliable dataset-specific interpolation weight can be estimated from a modest subset of the target distribution, without requiring evaluation on the full benchmark.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A11.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This analysis is separate from the protocol used in the main results, where <math id="A11.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected once on the CC3M validation set and then fixed for evaluation on Flickr30k, COCO, and NoCaps.
Its purpose is to assess a complementary scenario in which a small subset from the deployment distribution is available.
In this setting, the results indicate that such a subset is sufficient to estimate a reliable dataset-specific SLERP weight.</p>
</div>
</section>

Fig. <a href="#A12.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Appendix L Additional Flip Analyses ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> presents the corresponding NoCaps analysis for both T2I and I2T retrieval.
In all plots, <math id="A12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the old-model query representation, whereas <math id="A12.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the SVD-aligned new-model query representation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A12.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A12.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These additional results are consistent with the trend observed in Fig. <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Compatibility Results ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.
The optimal interpolation weight is governed by the balance between positive and negative flips, rather than by the positive-flip rate alone.
Across retrieval directions and datasets, SLERP improves Recall@1 when it corrects more previously incorrect queries than it causes previously correct queries to fail.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A13" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix M </span>Per-Query Oracle Analysis</h2>

<div id="A13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The geometric characterization in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> is formulated with respect to an idealized retrieval-optimal direction <math id="A13.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is not observable in practice.
We therefore complement it with an empirical analysis at the level of individual queries, asking whether interior points of the evaluated SLERP arc provide retrieval benefits that neither endpoint provides.
This analysis uses query-level test labels and is intended only as an oracle upper bound; it does not constitute a deployable weight-selection procedure.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A13.F11" class="ltx_figure">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A13.F11.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="A13.F11.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Per-query oracle analysis on Flickr30k image-to-text retrieval for CLIP ViT-L/14 <math id="A13.F11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32 with text-only alignment.
<span id="A13.F11.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Distribution of per-query oracle interpolation weights, where each query is assigned the weight attaining the best rank of its highest-ranked relevant item, with ties broken by the highest relevant-item similarity and then by proximity to <math id="A13.F11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
Queries are divided into those for which Recall@1 is achievable at some interpolation weight (blue, <math id="A13.F11.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=18{,}344" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18,344</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=18{,}344</annotation></semantics></math>) and those for which it is not (gray, <math id="A13.F11.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=12{,}670" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12,670</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=12{,}670</annotation></semantics></math>); shaded columns mark the two endpoints of the interpolation path.
<span id="A13.F11.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Recall@1 obtained with a single fixed interpolation weight applied to all queries, maximized at the dataset-level optimum <math id="A13.F11.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
<span id="A13.F11.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> Cosine similarity between the interpolated query and its highest-scoring relevant item at each weight, averaged over Recall@1-achievable queries.
Red dashed and cyan dotted lines mark the dataset oracle <math id="A13.F11.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> and the CC3M-selected weight <math id="A13.F11.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}=0.7</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.
Because most successful queries attain rank one over many weights, the oracle distribution follows the relevant-item similarity and peaks at <math id="A13.F11.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than at the Recall@1-optimal fixed weight <math id="A13.F11.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A13.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We consider Flickr30k image-to-text retrieval for CLIP ViT-L/14 <math id="A13.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32 with text-only Procrustes alignment, evaluated on the grid <math id="A13.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}=\{0,0.1,\ldots,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}=\{0,0.1,\ldots,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A13.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0</annotation></semantics></math> is the old-model query and <math id="A13.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> is the SVD-aligned new-model query.
For each query <math id="A13.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\mathcal{Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\mathcal{Q}</annotation></semantics></math> and weight <math id="A13.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A13.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}(\alpha)\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}(\alpha)\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate whether a relevant caption is retrieved at rank one, and let <math id="A13.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the cosine similarity between the interpolated query and its highest-scoring relevant caption.
We distinguish two quantities: <math id="A13.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> measures retrieval success and depends on all gallery items, whereas <math id="A13.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> measures proximity to the relevant item alone.</p>
</div>
<div id="A13.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The per-query oracle Recall@1 selects the best weight independently for each query,</p>
<table id="A13.E119" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A13.E119.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{R@1}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{Q}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{Q}}\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal{A}}c_{i}(\alpha)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mn>1</mn><mi>PQ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{R@1}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{Q}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{Q}}\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal{A}}c_{i}(\alpha).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(119)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A13.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Among the <math id="A13.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31{,}014" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31,014</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31{,}014</annotation></semantics></math> Flickr30k image queries, <math id="A13.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18{,}344" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18,344</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18{,}344</annotation></semantics></math> achieve Recall@1 for at least one weight, giving <math id="A13.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{R@1}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=59.15\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mn>1</mn><mi>PQ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>59.15</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{R@1}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=59.15\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
To isolate the contribution of the interior of the arc, we compare it with an endpoint-only oracle that, for each query, may choose only between the old-model query and the SVD-aligned query, <math id="A13.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max\{c_{i}(0),c_{i}(1)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max\{c_{i}(0),c_{i}(1)\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This endpoint-only oracle reaches <math id="A13.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.61\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>54.61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.61\%</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A13.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16{,}936" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16,936</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16{,}936</annotation></semantics></math> queries).
The remaining <math id="A13.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}408" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,408</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}408</annotation></semantics></math> queries achieve Recall@1 exclusively at interior weights, so interior points account for a gain of <math id="A13.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.54" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.54</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.54</annotation></semantics></math> Recall@1 points that no per-query choice between the two endpoints can recover.
Beyond rank one, for <math id="A13.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6{,}647" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6,647</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6{,}647</annotation></semantics></math> queries (<math id="A13.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21.43\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>21.43</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21.43\%</annotation></semantics></math>) the best relevant-item rank attained at an interior weight is strictly better than the best rank attained at either endpoint.</p>
</div>
<div id="A13.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p4.1" class="ltx_p">As Recall@1 is a thresholded event, most successful queries remain successful over a wide range of weights: <math id="A13.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.57\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96.57</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.57\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the Recall@1-achievable queries are retrieved at rank one for more than one weight (<math id="A13.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.53" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.53</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.53</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="A13.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> weights on average), including <math id="A13.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8{,}873" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8,873</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8{,}873</annotation></semantics></math> queries retrieved at rank one for every weight.
For such queries, Recall@1 alone does not identify a preferred position along the arc.</p>
</div>
<div id="A13.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The relevant-item similarity <math id="A13.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> provides a direct observable counterpart of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Angular retrieval gap along the SLERP arc; proof in Appendix ). ‣ 3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.
Instantiating <math id="A13.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math> as the normalized embedding of a relevant caption <math id="A13.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Angular retrieval gap along the SLERP arc; proof in Appendix ). ‣ 3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> gives <math id="A13.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle q_{\alpha},g\rangle=\rho\cos(\alpha\theta-\psi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>ψ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle q_{\alpha},g\rangle=\rho\cos(\alpha\theta-\psi)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, if the similarity to <math id="A13.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> at some interior grid weight strictly exceeds its values at both endpoints, the in-plane projection of <math id="A13.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> lies in the relative interior of the minor arc from <math id="A13.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A13.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math>.
We observe this for <math id="A13.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.87\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.87</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.87\%</annotation></semantics></math> of all queries: for nearly every query, the similarity to at least one relevant caption is maximized strictly inside the arc.
Averaged over Recall@1-achievable queries, <math id="A13.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> peaks at <math id="A13.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas the fixed-weight Recall@1 peaks at <math id="A13.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> (Figs. <a href="#A13.F11.sf2" title="In Figure 11 ‣ Appendix M Per-Query Oracle Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11(b)</span></a> and <a href="#A13.F11.sf3" title="In Figure 11 ‣ Appendix M Per-Query Oracle Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11(c)</span></a>), since retrieval success also depends on how the similarities to non-relevant items change along the arc.</p>
</div>
<div id="A13.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To assign a single oracle weight to each query, we select the weight with the best relevant-item rank; ties are broken by the highest relevant-item similarity <math id="A13.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math>, and any remaining tie in favor of the weight closest to <math id="A13.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
Fig. <a href="#A13.F11.sf1" title="In Figure 11 ‣ Appendix M Per-Query Oracle Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11(a)</span></a> shows the resulting distribution.
Because most successful queries are tied in rank over many weights, the similarity criterion determines their oracle weight, and the distribution follows the relevant-item similarity: it peaks at <math id="A13.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.3</annotation></semantics></math> rather than at <math id="A13.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{\star}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{\star}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> or at the CC3M-selected <math id="A13.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}=0.7</annotation></semantics></math>.
Under this rule, <math id="A13.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17{,}912" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17,912</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17{,}912</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="A13.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18{,}344" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18,344</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18{,}344</annotation></semantics></math> Recall@1-achievable queries (<math id="A13.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.65\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>97.65</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.65\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and <math id="A13.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of all queries are assigned an interior weight.
These fractions reflect where the relevant-item similarity is maximized among rank-optimal weights and should not be read as the fraction of queries that require interpolation to succeed, which is given by the <math id="A13.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}408" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,408</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}408</annotation></semantics></math> interior-only queries above.</p>
</div>
