<div id="A13.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Tab. <a href="#A13.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Appendix M Per-Query Oracle Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> summarizes the resulting upper bounds.
The per-query oracle reaches <math id="A13.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.15\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>59.15</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.15\%</annotation></semantics></math> I2T Recall@1, compared with <math id="A13.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40.62\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40.62</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40.62\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the old model, <math id="A13.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42.89\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>42.89</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42.89\%</annotation></semantics></math> for SVD alignment alone, <math id="A13.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48.00\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>48.00</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.00\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the fixed CC3M-selected weight, and <math id="A13.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48.61\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>48.61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.61\%</annotation></semantics></math> for the dataset-level oracle weight.
Part of this gain comes from choosing, per query, between the two endpoints (<math id="A13.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.61\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>54.61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.61\%</annotation></semantics></math>); the remaining <math id="A13.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.54" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.54</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.54</annotation></semantics></math> points are attainable only at interior weights.
The per-query oracle also exceeds the <math id="A13.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48.72\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>48.72</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.72\%</annotation></semantics></math> obtained by fully re-indexing with CLIP ViT-L/14; this comparison should not be interpreted as a deployable advantage, since the oracle uses query-level test labels to select a different weight for each query.</p>
</div>
<div id="A13.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A13.p8.1" class="ltx_p">This experiment does not recover <math id="A13.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math> itself.
It tests two observable counterparts of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Angular retrieval gap along the SLERP arc; proof in Appendix ). ‣ 3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.
First, instantiating <math id="A13.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math> as a relevant item, the interior condition of the theorem holds for <math id="A13.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.87\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.87</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.87\%</annotation></semantics></math> of queries, indicating that the residual direction between the old-model and aligned new-model queries consistently moves the query closer to its relevant items.
Second, at the level of the discrete retrieval event, interior weights yield Recall@1 successes unavailable at either endpoint for <math id="A13.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}408" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,408</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}408</annotation></semantics></math> queries and strictly improve the best relevant-item rank for <math id="A13.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21.43\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>21.43</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21.43\%</annotation></semantics></math> of queries.
Whether a higher relevant-item similarity translates into a retrieval gain depends on the margin to non-relevant items, consistent with the margin-based certification in Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Connection Between SLERP and Recall@𝐾 ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.
Finally, the gap between the per-query oracle and the fixed support-set-selected weight indicates that the preferred interpolation position varies across queries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A14" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix N </span>Alignment and Endpoint-Combination Baselines</h2>

<div id="A14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To identify the source of the improvements observed in the main experiments, we decompose the proposed approach into its three components: the alignment map, the operator that combines the two query representations, and the selection of the interpolation position.
We compare orthogonal Procrustes with non-isometric alignment maps, and SLERP with alternative ways of combining the old-model query <math id="A14.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and the aligned new-model query <math id="A14.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math>.
The old-model gallery is always left unchanged throughout the analysis.</p>
</div>
<div id="A14.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All results cover the five model pairs, three retrieval datasets, three alignment-support modalities, and both retrieval directions of Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, i.e., <math id="A14.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math> configurations and <math id="A14.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90</annotation></semantics></math> compatibility evaluations.
Every alignment map, regularization parameter, and interpolation parameter is estimated or selected only on the CC3M validation split used as alignment support set, separately for I2T and T2I Recall@1, and then used for evaluation on Flickr30k, COCO, and NoCaps.
Interpolation coefficients are selected over the grid <math id="A14.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,0.1,\ldots,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,0.1,\ldots,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Compatibility is assessed with the empirical protocol of Eq. <a href="#S4.E15" title="In 4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A14.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">N.1 </span>Alignment baselines</h3>

<div id="A14.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A14.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{a}\times d_{\mathrm{new}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>new</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{a}\times d_{\mathrm{new}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{a}\times d_{\mathrm{old}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U\in\mathbb{R}^{N_{a}\times d_{\mathrm{old}}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the support-set embeddings of Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
Each map below replaces the orthogonal Procrustes map <math id="A14.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> used in our approach; the resulting query is normalized before retrieval, and no interpolation is applied.</p>
</div>

<p id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and the normalized aligned query is <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v=(\bar{v}A^{\star}+b^{\star\top})/\|\bar{v}A^{\star}+b^{\star\top}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>⋆</mo><mo lspace="0em">⁣</mo><mo>⊤</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>⋆</mo><mo lspace="0em">⁣</mo><mo>⊤</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v=(\bar{v}A^{\star}+b^{\star\top})/\|\bar{v}A^{\star}+b^{\star\top}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Ridge alignment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib84" title="" class="ltx_ref">84</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The same map is fitted with Tikhonov regularization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib85" title="" class="ltx_ref">85</a>]</cite>,</p>

<p id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\in\{10^{-6},10^{-4}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\in\{10^{-6},10^{-4}\}</annotation></semantics></math> selected directly on the support set.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">One-sided CCA.</h4>

<div id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The new-model embeddings are projected onto <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{old}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>old</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{old}}</annotation></semantics></math> canonical directions with covariance regularization <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\in\{10^{-6},10^{-4}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\in\{10^{-6},10^{-4}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, while the old-model side is kept in its original coordinates so that the gallery remains unchanged. This is a special case of standard CCA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">86</a>]</cite>.
With an untransformed target, the canonical projection followed by the least-squares map to the old coordinates reduces to regularized regression; one-sided CCA therefore coincides with ridge alignment, and indeed produces identical results in all <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math> configurations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Whitened Procrustes.</h4>

<div id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both embedding sets are centered and whitened with <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>-regularized covariances before solving the orthogonal Procrustes problem, and the aligned query is mapped back to the old-model coordinates and normalized; <math id="A14.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\in\{10^{-4},10^{-2},10^{-1},1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\in\{10^{-4},10^{-2},10^{-1},1\}</annotation></semantics></math> is selected on the support set.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A14.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">N.2 </span>Endpoint-combination baselines</h3>

<div id="A14.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All combination methods use the same orthogonally aligned endpoint <math id="A14.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> obtained with Procrustes.</p>
</div>
<section id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">

<div id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The simplest combination uses no weight selection:</p>

<p id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We obtain</p>

As shown in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Relationship Between SLERP and NLERP ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>, NLERP and SLERP traverse the same minor geodesic between <math id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> under a monotone reparameterization: SLERP is linear in angular displacement, whereas the angular position associated with an NLERP coefficient depends on the query-specific endpoint angle.</p>
</div>
</section>

For a fixed query, the normalization in Eq. <a href="#A14.E123" title="In Normalized linear interpolation. ‣ N.2 Endpoint-combination baselines ‣ Appendix N Alignment and Endpoint-Combination Baselines ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">123</span></a> rescales all gallery scores by the same positive constant, so score interpolation, score ensembling, and NLERP at the same coefficient induce identical rankings.</p>

<section id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Query-adaptive NLERP.</h4>

<div id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To test whether a query-dependent position helps, the coefficient is predicted from the endpoint agreement of each query,</p>

</table>
<p id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is the logistic function and <math id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(b_{m},s_{m})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(b_{m},s_{m})</annotation></semantics></math> are selected separately for image and text queries on CC3M over <math id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{m}\in\{-3,-1.5,0,1.5,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{m}\in\{-3,-1.5,0,1.5,3\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{m}\in\{-3,0,3,6\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{m}\in\{-3,0,3,6\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The rule uses no test labels: at inference it only requires the cosine between the two endpoints, which is available at negligible cost.</p>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A14.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">

<td id="A14.T10.5.13.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.5pt;padding-right:2.5pt;"><span id="A14.T10.5.13.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">37.42</span></td>
<td id="A14.T10.5.13.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.5pt;padding-right:2.5pt;"><span id="A14.T10.5.13.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">+4.89</span></td>

</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A14.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tab. <a href="#A14.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ N.3 Discussion ‣ Appendix N Alignment and Endpoint-Combination Baselines ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows that orthogonal Procrustes is the strongest alignment method among the evaluated ones.
The non-isometric maps, although more flexible on the support set, generalize substantially worse to the target benchmarks: affine alignment loses <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15.35</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.35</annotation></semantics></math> mean Recall@1 points relative to Procrustes, ridge regression and one-sided CCA lose <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11.32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.32</annotation></semantics></math>, and whitened Procrustes loses <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.83</annotation></semantics></math>, with compatibility dropping from <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45/90</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="37/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>37</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">37/90</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.
Because these maps rescale or shear the new-model representation, they distort the inner-product geometry that retrieval relies on, whereas an isometry preserves it.
The table also shows that alignment alone is not sufficient: SVD remains below the unchanged old-model query by <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.64</annotation></semantics></math> I2T and <math id="A14.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.49</annotation></semantics></math> T2I Recall@1 points on average, which is why it satisfies compatibility in only half of the evaluations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A14.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Replacing the SVD endpoint by the fixed normalized midpoint raises mean I2T and T2I Recall@1 from <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="51.72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>51.72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">51.72</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="33.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>33.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">33.77</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57.76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57.76</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="37.23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>37.23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">37.23</annotation></semantics></math>, a mean improvement of <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.75</annotation></semantics></math> points over SVD.
Relative to the unchanged old-model query, it improves I2T and T2I Recall@1 by <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.40</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.97</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.97</annotation></semantics></math> points, and it increases compatibility from <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45/90</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A14.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>72</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72/90</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since this baseline has no tunable weight and uses no validation data, this gain is attributable to the combination of the two endpoints.</p>
</div>
<div id="A14.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Support-set selected interpolation substantially improves compatibility robustness.
SLERP improves mean Recall@1 over SVD by <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.80</annotation></semantics></math> points, only <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math> more than the midpoint, while raising compatibility from <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>72</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72/90</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84/90</annotation></semantics></math>; relative to the old-model query, it improves I2T and T2I Recall@1 by <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.36</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.36</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.12</annotation></semantics></math> points.
Support-set selected NLERP reaches <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.81" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.81</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.81</annotation></semantics></math> points and <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84/90</annotation></semantics></math>, and score interpolation matches it, as expected from their ranking equivalence.<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
              
              
              
            In one configuration the selected coefficient coincides with the old-model endpoint, where floating-point ties change the outcome of a single query; we count it as non-compatible, consistent with NLERP.</span></span></span>
Query-adaptive NLERP gives the best results, <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.89</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.89</annotation></semantics></math> points and <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88/90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88/90</annotation></semantics></math>, but improves mean Recall@1 by only <math id="A14.SS3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.09</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.09</annotation></semantics></math> points over SLERP while requiring four additional calibrated parameters; its higher compatibility nevertheless indicates that query-dependent positions are a promising direction, consistent with the per-query oracle analysis in Appendix <a href="#A13" title="Appendix M Per-Query Oracle Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">M</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A14.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A14.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The ablation separates the two sources of improvement. Combining the old-model query with the orthogonally aligned new-model query accounts for most of the mean Recall@1 improvement, while validation-based position selection makes these improvements consistently satisfy the backward-compatibility criterion across model pairs, datasets, support modalities, and retrieval directions.
Similar improvements are observed with SLERP, NLERP, and score interpolation, indicating that they arise from exploiting the residual post-alignment geometry rather than from a particular combination operator.
We adopt SLERP as the canonical parameterization because <math id="A14.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\angle(u,q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{slerp}})=\alpha\,\angle(u,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>α</mi><mi>slerp</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\angle(u,q_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{slerp}})=\alpha\,\angle(u,v)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A14.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> represents the same fraction of the angular displacement from the old-model query toward the aligned new-model query for every query. This constant-angular-speed property is precisely what the characterization in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> relies on. Under NLERP or score interpolation, by contrast, the angular position associated with a fixed coefficient depends on the query-specific angle between the endpoints.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A15" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix O </span>Limitations</h2>

<section id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Selection of the interpolation weight.</h4>

<div id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SLERP requires selecting an interpolation weight along the geodesic arc between the old-model query embedding and the SVD-aligned new-model query embedding.
The optimal value is not known a priori and must be estimated from data, either from the deployment distribution or from a separate support set.
In the main experiments, we avoid target-set tuning by selecting <math id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> on the CC3M alignment support set and applying the same value to Flickr30k, COCO, and NoCaps.
The target-set budget analysis in Appendix <a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Target-Set Budget Sensitivity ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a> shows that, when a small labeled subset from the deployment distribution is available, a reliable interpolation weight can be estimated from only a modest number of examples.
At the same time, the retrieval results in Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and the zero-shot classification results in Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Cross-Modal Zero-shot Classification ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a> show that SLERP is robust to this choice: support-set selected weights transfer well across target datasets and remain close to the best dataset-specific performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Query-side computation.</h4>

<div id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SLERP requires no compatibility training and leaves the deployed gallery unchanged, but it needs both endpoint representations at inference time: the old-model query embedding and the SVD-aligned new-model query embedding.
Compared with using a single encoder, SLERP therefore adds query-side computation and requires both encoders, or suitable cached representations, to be available during deployment.
This overhead is independent of the gallery size: the existing gallery remains indexed in the old-model space, and only incoming queries require the additional computation.
A full model upgrade, by contrast, requires re-encoding and re-indexing the entire gallery before the new model can be used directly.
In practice, SLERP is best viewed as a compatibility mechanism for the migration period (Appendix <a href="#A16" title="Appendix P Deployment Cost and Migration-Period Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">P</span></a>) following a model update, keeping the old index usable while full gallery re-indexing proceeds offline.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dependence on endpoint quality.</h4>

<div id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A15.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our method requires neither model retraining nor gradient-based optimization: it does not update either encoder, learn dataset-specific correction layers, or optimize compatibility losses on the target benchmarks. Its only fitted components are the closed-form Procrustes map and the interpolation weight, both estimated on the alignment support set.
Consequently, its performance depends on the quality and complementarity of the old-model query embedding, the new-model query embedding, and the estimated Procrustes map.
If both endpoint representations are weak for a deployment domain, interpolation alone cannot introduce new task-specific information.
The same property that limits the method also supports its transfer: because nothing is fitted to a specific target benchmark, the same support-set-selected weight carries over across retrieval benchmarks and to zero-shot classification with fixed old-model text prototypes.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A16" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix P </span>Deployment Cost and Migration-Period Analysis</h2>

<div id="A16.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A16.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix quantifies the practical cost of the proposed approach.
We first analyze the query-side computation and latency required by SLERP queries against the old-model gallery, and relate them to the cost of full gallery re-indexing.
We then evaluate SLERP during the migration period, in which the gallery is progressively re-encoded with the new aligned model, and compare it with partial gallery backfilling. Unless otherwise stated, we consider the CLIP ViT-L/14 <math id="A16.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32 upgrade with text-only Procrustes support.</p>
</div>
<section id="A16.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A16.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A16.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SLERP requires both the old-model query embedding <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and the SVD-aligned new-model query embedding <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> for every incoming query.
Its main cost is therefore the evaluation of the two encoders, whereas the remaining operations are negligible.
According to the OpenCLIP profiles, the ViT-B/32 image and text encoders require <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.82</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.96</annotation></semantics></math> GFLOPs per input, respectively, while the corresponding ViT-L/14 encoders require <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="162.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>162.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">162.03</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13.30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.30</annotation></semantics></math> GFLOPs.
By comparison, the <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="768\times 512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>768</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">768\times 512</annotation></semantics></math> Procrustes projection requires <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="393{,}216" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>393,216</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">393{,}216</annotation></semantics></math> multiply-accumulate operations, or approximately <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.79</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.79</annotation></semantics></math> MFLOPs, and the spherical interpolation operation is linear in the embedding dimension.
The gallery, its index, and the complexity of approximate nearest-neighbor search are left unchanged, since each query remains a single <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{old}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>old</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{old}}</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional unit vector searched against the old-model index.
Aggregated over <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> queries and a gallery of <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{7}</annotation></semantics></math> items, the encoder compute of SLERP amounts to <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17.09</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17.09</annotation></semantics></math> PFLOPs for I2T and <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.93</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.93</annotation></semantics></math> PFLOPs for T2I retrieval, compared with <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.88" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.88</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.88</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.60</annotation></semantics></math> PFLOPs for old-model queries.
Full re-indexing followed by new-model queries instead requires <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="149.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>149.20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">149.20</annotation></semantics></math> PFLOPs and <math id="A16.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.62</annotation></semantics></math> EFLOPs, respectively, the latter being dominated by the re-encoding of the image gallery.</p>
</div>
<div id="A16.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A16.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Tab. <a href="#A16.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ P.1 Query-Side Cost and Re-indexing Trade-off ‣ Appendix P Deployment Cost and Migration-Period Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> reports the corresponding query latency, measured on an NVIDIA A100 with an IVF-PQ index built over <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{7}</annotation></semantics></math> synthetic gallery vectors.
When the two encoders are evaluated sequentially on a single GPU, SLERP increases the latency by approximately <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.4</annotation></semantics></math> ms relative to the fully re-indexed system.
Since <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> are computed independently, the two encoders can be executed concurrently, reducing the encoding latency from <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\mathrm{old}}+\phi_{\mathrm{new}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>new</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\mathrm{old}}+\phi_{\mathrm{new}}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max(\phi_{\mathrm{old}},\phi_{\mathrm{new}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>new</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max(\phi_{\mathrm{old}},\phi_{\mathrm{new}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
With the encoders placed on separate GPUs, or when the old-model query embedding is cached, the gap to the fully re-indexed system reduces to approximately <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math> ms.
In all configurations, the projection and interpolation stages contribute less than <math id="A16.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> ms, and the overhead is dominated by encoder inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A16.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">P.2 </span>Migration Period with Partial Backfilling</h3>

<figure id="A16.F12" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.39836v1/backfill_i2t.svg" id="A16.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/195;" width="476" height="195"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A16.F12.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="A16.F12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Image-to-text Recall@1 during partial backfilling of the text gallery on Flickr30k, with text-only Procrustes support.
The partial-backfill baseline issues SVD-aligned new-model queries against a mixed gallery in which an increasing fraction of old-model caption embeddings is replaced by new-model embeddings.
At <math id="A16.F12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\%</annotation></semantics></math>, the baseline coincides with the SVD query on the fixed old-model gallery (square), and at <math id="A16.F12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math> with full re-indexing (star).
SVD+SLERP uses the CC3M-selected <math id="A16.F12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> and leaves the gallery unchanged.
Shaded regions mark backfilling fractions at which the baseline falls below the old-model system and thus violates Eq. <a href="#S4.E15" title="In 4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A16.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A16.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In practice, large galleries are rarely re-encoded at once; instead, they are backfilled progressively while the system remains in service <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>.
We therefore compare SLERP with partial gallery backfilling for image-to-text retrieval on Flickr30k.
In the partial-backfill baseline, a random fraction <math id="A16.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in\{0\%,10\%,\ldots,100\%\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in\{0\%,10\%,\ldots,100\%\}</annotation></semantics></math> of the captions is re-encoded with the new model, while the remaining captions retain their old-model embeddings, and queries are computed with the aligned new-model encoder.
Consequently, <math id="A16.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=0\%</annotation></semantics></math> recovers the SVD baseline with a fixed old-model gallery, and <math id="A16.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=100\%</annotation></semantics></math> recovers full re-indexing.
SLERP, instead, uses the CC3M-selected <math id="A16.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> of Tab. <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and leaves the gallery entirely unchanged. We report the results of the analysis in Fig. <a href="#A16.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ P.2 Migration Period with Partial Backfilling ‣ Appendix P Deployment Cost and Migration-Period Analysis ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> for CLIP ViT-L/14 <math id="A16.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32 and SigLIP2 <math id="A16.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> SigLIP1 model pairs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A16.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A16.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For CLIP ViT-L/14 <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> CLIP ViT-B/32, SLERP matches or exceeds partial backfilling at every evaluated fraction below full re-indexing.
Without re-encoding any gallery item, SLERP reaches <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>48.00</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.00</annotation></semantics></math> Recall@1, whereas partial backfilling requires re-encoding <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>90</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the text gallery (<math id="A16.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="139{,}563" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>139,563</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">139{,}563</annotation></semantics></math> captions) to reach <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="47.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>47.98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">47.98</annotation></semantics></math>.
Relative to the old model, SLERP thus recovers <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="91.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>91.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">91.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the improvement obtained by full re-indexing (<math id="A16.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48.72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>48.72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.72</annotation></semantics></math>).
For SigLIP2 <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> SigLIP1, the SVD-aligned query falls far below the old model (<math id="A16.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45.46" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45.46</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45.46</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58.09</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.09</annotation></semantics></math>), and partial backfilling exceeds the old model only once <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the text gallery has been re-encoded.
SLERP, in contrast, satisfies the compatibility criterion (<math id="A16.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58.63</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.63</annotation></semantics></math>) with an unchanged gallery, and partial backfilling surpasses it only once between <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A16.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the captions have been re-encoded.</p>
</div>
<div id="A16.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A16.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As backfilling progresses, direct retrieval with the new model becomes preferable, and once re-indexing is complete, the old encoder can be retired.
Combining SLERP queries for non-backfilled items with new-model queries for backfilled items is a natural extension of this analysis, also supported by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib87" title="" class="ltx_ref">87</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
