<div id="Ax2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="Ax2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="Ax2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Claims</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The abstract and introduction accurately describe the paper’s contributions and scope: a training-free query-side SLERP method after orthogonal Procrustes alignment for backward-compatible VLM retrieval. The stated theoretical claims are developed in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Connection Between SLERP and Recall@𝐾 ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>, and the empirical claims are supported by experiments across CLIP, SigLIP, and SigLIP2 on Flickr30k, COCO, and NoCaps in Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A <span id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span> or <span id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Limitations</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper includes an introduction to the limitations discussion in Sec. <a href="#S5" title="5 Conclusion ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> with a dedicated Appendix <a href="#A15" title="Appendix O Limitations ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">O</span></a>, covering interpolation-weight selection, the need to compute both old and new query embeddings at inference time, and the dependence of the training-free method on the quality of the endpoint representations and Procrustes alignment.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper has no limitation while the answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span> means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix8.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theory assumptions and proofs</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix10" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix11" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper states the assumptions for the geometric analysis in Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Geometric Characterization of Spherical Interpolation for Compatible Retrieval ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, including normalized embeddings and the non-degenerate condition. The main theoretical results are demonstrated in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Proof of Theorem ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>, and Appendices <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Decomposition of the Retrieval-Optimal Direction ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a> and <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Connection Between SLERP and Recall@𝐾 ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper does not include theoretical results.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix12.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experimental result reproducibility</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix13" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix13.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix14" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix14.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix14.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix15" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix15.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix15.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper uses closed-form alignment and interpolation procedures, and provides the details needed to reproduce the main experiments in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>. These include the public model checkpoints, datasets, alignment support set, support-modality choices, Procrustes/SVD alignment procedure, SLERP grid search for <math id="Ax2.I1.ix15.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, baselines, metrics, and compatibility criterion. The main results in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Compatibility Results ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> are further supported by detailed Recall@1/5/10 results and additional analyses in Appendices <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Detailed Retrieval Performance ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>, <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Cross-Modal Zero-shot Classification ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>, <a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Re-indexing ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>, and <a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Target-Set Budget Sensitivity ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper does not include experiments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the paper includes experiments, a <span id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span> answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example</p>
<ol id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(a)</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(b)</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(c)</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(d)</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix16.I1.i5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Open access to data and code</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix17" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix17.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix17.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix18" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix18.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix18.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix18.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix19" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix19.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix19.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The experiments use publicly available datasets and model checkpoints, and the paper describes the closed-form Procrustes/SVD alignment and SLERP evaluation protocol in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>. A minimal reference implementation of the proposed method is publicly available at <a href="https://github.com/miccunifi/SLERP_backward_compatibility" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/miccunifi/SLERP_backward_compatibility</a>. However, exact run commands and full reproduction scripts for the proposed method and baselines are not yet included; they will be released in the same repository.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that paper does not include experiments requiring code.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines (<a href="https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy</a>) for more details.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so <span id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span> is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines (<a href="https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy</a>) for more details.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix20.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experimental setting/details</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix21" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix21.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix21.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix22" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix22.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix22.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix22.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix23" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix23.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix23.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper specifies the experimental setting in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and Sec. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Evaluation Protocol ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>, including the evaluated model pairs, public checkpoints, datasets, CC3M alignment/validation split, support-modality choices, baselines, Recall@K metrics, compatibility criterion, and the SLERP grid used to select <math id="Ax2.I1.ix23.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>α</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since the proposed method is training-free and uses closed-form Procrustes/SVD alignment, no optimizer or training hyperparameters are required for the main method.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix24" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix24.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix24.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper does not include experiments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix24.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experiment statistical significance</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix25" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix25.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix25.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix26" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix26.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix26.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix26.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix27" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix27.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix27.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: Most of the main experiments are deterministic evaluations based on frozen pretrained models and closed-form Procrustes/SVD alignment, so the paper reports point estimates for the main retrieval and classification results. The only analysis involving randomness is the target-set budget sensitivity study in Appendix <a href="#A11" title="Appendix K Target-Set Budget Sensitivity ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K</span></a>, where target subsets are sampled with three random seeds and the paper reports the mean Recall@1 curve with shaded <math id="Ax2.I1.ix27.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> bands (see Fig. <a href="#A11.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix K Target-Set Budget Sensitivity ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper does not include experiments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span> if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix28.I1.i9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">8.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experiments compute resources</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix29" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix29.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix29.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix30" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix30.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix30.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix30.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix31" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix31.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix31.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper reports the experimental protocol, datasets, model checkpoints, and evaluation metrics, but it does not currently provide detailed compute-resource information such as GPU/CPU type or memory.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix32" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix32.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix32.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper does not include experiments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix32.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">9.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Code of ethics</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix33" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix33.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix33.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics <a href="https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines</a>?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix34" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix34.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix34.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix34.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">[Yes] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix35" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix35.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix35.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The research is conducted according to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix36" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix36.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix36.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the authors answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span>, they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix36.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i10" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">10.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Broader impacts</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix37" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix37.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix37.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix38" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix38.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix38.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix38.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix39" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix39.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix39.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper focuses on a technical method for backward-compatible vision-language retrieval and discusses practical limitations in Appendix <a href="#A15" title="Appendix O Limitations ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">O</span></a>, but it does not separately discuss both positive and negative societal impacts. Potential impacts include reducing the cost of model upgrades for retrieval systems, while possible risks include improving retrieval systems used in sensitive applications such as surveillance or biased content search.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that there is no societal impact of the work performed.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the authors answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> or <span id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span>, they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix40.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i11" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">11.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Safeguards</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix41" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix41.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix41.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix42" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix42.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix42.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix42.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix43" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix43.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix43.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper does not release new pretrained models, image generators, scraped datasets, or other assets with high misuse risk. Our work uses existing public pretrained vision-language models and benchmark datasets.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix44" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix44.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix44.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper poses no such risks.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix44.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i12" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">12.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Ax2.I1.i12.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Licenses for existing assets</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix45" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix45.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix45.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix46" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix46.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix46.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer: <span id="Ax2.I1.ix46.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF8000;">[No] </span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix47" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix47.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix47.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Justification: The paper uses existing assets, including public pretrained model checkpoints and benchmark datasets, and credits their original sources in Sec. <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experimental Results ‣ Spherical Interpolation for Backward-Compatible Multimodal Representations" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>. However, the current version does not explicitly list the licenses or terms of use for each dataset, model checkpoint, or code asset used in the experiments.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"></span>
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guidelines:</p>
<ul id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The answer <span id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">[N/A] </span> means that the paper does not use existing assets.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, <a href="https://paperswithcode.com/datasets" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">paperswithcode.com/datasets</a> has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Ax2.I1.ix48.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div></li>

    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
